title: Finish and evaluate our card pouch
outcome: TEXTILES: finish and evaluate a textile product.
half_term_outcomes: FOODWISE: plan a balanced meal on a budget.
FOODWISE: prepare a 2-3 step dish safely.
FOODWISE: evaluate taste, cost and nutrition.
TEXTILES: choose fabric and technique for a purpose.
TEXTILES: measure, cut and join accurately.
TEXTILES: finish and evaluate a textile product.
goal: I can finish my item safely, test its purpose and explain what the evidence shows.
success: I can complete or direct an agreed finishing action and record the help used.
I can test the pouch against its purpose and give my own evidence-based view.
I can check the six weekly outcomes honestly and choose a next step.
purpose: A small reusable pouch for three paper prompt cards, each 60 mm by 80 mm. The top stays open. It should hold the cards upright, have joined sides and bottom, contain no loose sharp parts and be comfortable to handle.
design: Default model: two fabric pieces, each 100 mm wide by 120 mm high. A seam line is 10 mm inside the left, right and bottom edges. Leave the top open. Default join is hand running stitch. Use each pupil’s actual approved design and any recorded change.
finishing_steps: Put tools down and compare the actual item with the design. The adult checks that the fabric, thread and any bonding route are suitable. Count and control all needles before work.

With the agreed support, secure loose thread ends. For a hand-stitch end, take a small stitch through both layers on the back. Leave a loop before pulling tight. Pass the needle through the loop and pull snug. Repeat once. Trim only the loose tail with agreed scissors. Do not cut the seam or fabric.
Return and count all needles and other tools. Check that no sharp parts remain in the item. Test only when it is safe. If adhesive was used, wait for its full labelled cure before testing.
tests: Place the actual three 60 mm by 80 mm paper cards into the pouch without forcing them.
Do all three fit? What did you see?
Hold the pouch upright and lift it gently over the table. Do not shake it or turn it upside down.
Do the joined sides and bottom hold during this gentle check?
Look at edges and joins. Check handling only after the adult clears the item.
Are loose threads secured and sharp parts removed? Is it comfortable to handle?
safety: The adult selects and supervises appropriate needles, scissors and tools for the actual fabric. Count needles out and back, keep them in a container and never put pins or needles in the mouth. Pause with tools down. For a missing or broken needle, stop, keep the area clear and let the adult recover and account for all parts and control disposal. Do not release or test the pouch until all sharp parts are accounted for. Do not test an uncured adhesive join. Use the actual label and adult approval; no cure time is invented.
fallback: Without an actual safe item, materials or tools, use a spoken, signed, paper or empty-hand model. Explain the finishing sequence and predict how a test would work. Label it simulation. Keep actual finishing and product testing pending. Use real earlier evidence for the six-week grid; do not fill gaps with the class model.

Supported: Use one finishing or test prompt at a time with an adult.
Complete or direct one agreed action. Record what you did and what the adult did.
Use a sentence start for your own test result and one next step.
Check one grid row at a time using real work or an honest gap.
Standard: Use the actual design and item to choose a finishing action.
Carry out the safe fit, upright hold and handling checks.
Explain one result, one improvement and the support used.
Check all six outcomes with actual evidence locations and comments.
Stretch: Finish the core work and record first.
Explain how one design choice helped the purpose.
Compare a real test result with your earlier prediction.
Choose one change. Say which evidence makes it useful.

vocabulary: Complete the agreed details and make the item ready to check.
What the item needs to do for its user.
A check that gives evidence about how the item works.
Use evidence to explain what worked and what could improve.
Fasten a loose end so it stays in place.
A truthful record of what actually happened.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Show one action and test at a time. Model the first step, then fade support. Keep the design and actual item side by side. Read grid outcomes aloud and chunk them into two groups of three.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Accept pointing, speech, signing or pupil-directed adult handling. Ask one short question and wait. An adult may scribe exact pupil words, read them back and allow correction.
adaptations.SEMH: Offer a private adult review and a calm pause with tools down. Unfinished work and gaps are recorded without ranking pupils. No public performance, personal disclosure or competition is required.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Use an appropriate agreed tool, prepared threaded needle or adult handling directed by the pupil. Offer visual checks without touch. Record the actual role rather than claiming an unperformed skill.
adaptations.EAL: Rehearse in any language. Pair the word with the actual action or item. Offer a short sentence start. Confirm meaning and read the pupil’s record back.

careers: Textile makers and quality-checking teams compare a finished item with the brief. They record real test results and use them to choose a useful improvement.
misconceptions: A neat item must meet its purpose.
Appearance is one feature. The actual cards and joined edges need the agreed checks.
A prediction is a test result.
Record a prediction as a prediction. A result comes from an actual safe test.
A tick means the whole award is complete.
The grid records evidence for weekly outcomes. It is not an award decision.
The adult’s finishing is my independent skill.
Keep pupil actions, directed adult handling and other support separate.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Our item and purpose
pupil: Find your design, item and earlier records.
Choose a safe finishing action with the adult.
Put tools down while you check the plan.
stages.teacher: This is the assessing week. Retrieve the actual W04 design and W05 item or unfinished work. If either is missing, record that truthfully. Read the small card-pouch purpose. The adult checks tools, controls and counts needles before issuing them. Confirm whether any adhesive has fully cured according to the actual label. A missing item or unresolved safety check uses simulation, with practical testing pending.
stages.check: Ask: What must the pouch do? Expect it to hold three 60 by 80 mm cards upright, with safe joined edges and comfortable handling. Re-read the purpose if the answer is only look nice.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Evidence or prediction
pupil: Which statement is a real result?
I think the cards will fit / I put three cards in and they fitted.
Use a safe test to check a prediction.
stages.teacher: Compare the two statements. The first is a prediction; the second claims an actual test and needs a truthful record. Explain that model statements are examples, not observations of a pupil’s item. Pupils may point, speak or sign. Keep any test not yet done marked pending.
stages.check: Expected: the second statement describes a result only if the pupil actually did the test. If uncertain, sort a second pair: I expect the seam to hold / I gently lifted the upright pouch and the seam held.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: A finishing action shown
pupil: Watch the agreed securing and trimming routine.
See how the adult counts tools back.
Keep sharp parts away from the test.
stages.teacher: Use a safe sample, not the pupil’s evidence. For running stitch, demonstrate a small securing stitch through both layers on the back. Leave a loop before pulling tight, then pass the needle through it, pull snug and repeat once. Keep fingers clear of the needle exit. Demonstrate trimming the loose tail only with agreed scissors. Return the needle to its container and count it back. Show an unfinished edge and explain why it is not ready. Fade the model by asking the pupil to name the next safety action.
stages.check: Ask: Can we test with a needle still in the item? Expect no, stop and get the adult to remove and account for it. If not secure, keep tools with the adult and use directed handling.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Finish with the agreed support
pupil: Complete or direct your agreed finishing action.
Check joins and loose ends against the design.
Return and count tools before testing.
stages.teacher: Supervise the approved finishing action or let the pupil direct adult handling. The actual design controls the join. An adhesive route follows the actual label and full cure; it is not assessed as hand stitching. Keep the top open for this default pouch. Record exactly which actions the pupil and adult completed. Stop safely if time or skill support is insufficient. Begin clearing progressively.
stages.check: Look for a real action, secured loose ends or an accurately recorded unfinished part. Record support. Do not infer an independent stitch from the adult’s work.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: A safe test decision
pupil: A needle is still in the pouch.
Choose: test now, hide it in the seam, or stop for the adult’s removal and count.
Test only after the item is cleared.
stages.teacher: Correct hinge response is stop for adult removal and count. If any pupil chooses otherwise, stop their testing and reteach before restart. Parallel check: a bonded seam has not reached its full labelled cure; leave the test pending and wait. A correct quiz response does not itself clear the actual item. The adult checks the item, tools and joining method.
stages.check: All pupils identify stop-and-clear before testing. Recheck with the uncured seam example if needed. Only an actual adult safety check permits testing.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: Test and evaluate my item
pupil: Try the three cards without forcing them.
Hold the cleared pouch upright and lift gently.
Record actual results, one improvement and the help used.
stages.teacher: The independent stage still has agreed adult supervision. Use the actual three paper cards, each 60 by 80 mm. Check fit without force, upright gentle hold, joined edges and comfortable handling. No upside-down or shaking test is needed. Record the actual result or pending status. The pupil supplies their own evaluation and prioritised improvement. Adult scribing is read back. A missing item uses a prediction labelled simulation, not a result.
stages.check: Look for evidence linked to the purpose: what happened, what it shows, and one useful next action. Accept an honest failed or incomplete test with reasoning. Do not reward invented success.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Six outcomes and real evidence
pupil: Check the six weekly outcomes with your work.
Choose Shown, More to do or Not yet seen.
Add a real evidence location and a short comment.
stages.teacher: Use both pages of the Evidence Sheet, including the six-outcome tick-and-comment grid. The pupil confirms their own evaluation; the adult checks actual evidence and support. Food evidence comes from the earlier records, not a new claim or a taste inferred from a photo. A gap stays visible. A tick records weekly evidence, not qualification completion. Count and store all tools and clear the area.
stages.check: A chosen status needs a brief comment and actual location or honest gap. Keep pupil words and adult observations separate. No automatic whole-term pass is generated.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My next step and evidence
pupil: My item meets / partly meets / does not yet meet the purpose because ___.
One useful next step is ___.
My evidence is in ___.
stages.teacher: Confirm the item, design, test record, evaluation, grid and book locations. Let the pupil correct the words. Record unresolved finishing or testing as pending and agree a supported next opportunity if needed. This closes the six-week strand. No later lesson or award completion is claimed.
stages.check: Accept the pupil’s own evidence-based view through writing, speech, signing or exact confirmed scribing. A realistic next step can follow any outcome, including an unfinished item.
